idiom_name: int with_x(args, int (*body)(T *, void *), void *ctx) plus one cleanup label
implementation_notes: C has neither destructors nor a bracket statement, so the classic structure is written by hand: acquire the resource, invoke the caller's function pointer with the resource and a void* context that carries the captured state, and funnel every failure path through a single cleanup label so teardown runs exactly once. What replaces the Smalltalk block is the function pointer plus the context struct; what replaces the language-level guarantee is the discipline of a single exit label - every new return statement that bypasses it is a code-sandwich defect. Keep the wrapper when the pair repeats or when policy (retry, logging, admission) must be centralized; for a single call site the plain acquire-use-release sequence with one cleanup label is smaller.
pitfalls: The context pointer is the only way to pass captured state; the wrapper's cleanup label cannot know about anything the body allocated, so the body must own that or the contract must say who frees it.
A new early return inserted between setup and the cleanup label silently skips teardown - the discipline of one exit path is the whole guarantee, and the compiler does not enforce it.
The resource handle must be initialised before the first failure path reaches cleanup, or teardown runs on an indeterminate value.

variants.name: POSIX cancellation clean-up handler (pthread_cleanup_push / pop)
variants.implementation_notes: The only resource-bracketing facility in C's standard libraries: push a handler as part of the setup and pop it as the teardown, and the handler runs when the thread is cancelled or exits through pthread_exit, or when pop is called with a nonzero execute argument. The POSIX specification permits both to be macros that expand to an opening and a closing brace, so the pair must sit in the same lexical scope, and the man page warns that leaving the bracket with return, break, continue or goto is undefined behaviour - which is why this is a partial realization for cancellation-safety, not a general execute-around. Use it inside thread start functions where cancellation must not leave a lock held; keep the function-pointer wrapper above for ordinary exit paths.
pitfalls: The handler runs on cancellation and pthread_exit, not on an ordinary return: leaving the bracketed block any other way is undefined by POSIX, so it cannot be the wrapper's only guarantee.
On glibc both calls expand to braces, so declarations inside the bracket live in a nested scope and any control statement that jumps across the two macros is invalid.
longjmp out of the bracket (or from inside the handler) is undefined unless the jump buffer was filled inside the handler itself.
